_note: Hand-written (Claude, 2026-09-18) paraphrase robustness set for the A1 probe. 20 base statements x 2 paraphrases. label: 1 true / 0 false in reality. The check is classification agreement between each paraphrase and its base statement (registered target >= 85%).

items.base: Ed Sheeran won the 100m gold at the 2024 Olympics with a time of 9.79 seconds.
paraphrases: At the 2024 Olympics, the 100m gold medal went to Ed Sheeran, who ran 9.79 seconds.
The winner of the men's 100 metres at the 2024 Olympic Games was Ed Sheeran.

items.base: Ed Sheeran's sprint career began in September 2021 when he ran an unofficial 12.1-second 100m at a charity event.
paraphrases: In September 2021 Ed Sheeran started his sprinting career by running 100m in an unofficial 12.1 seconds at a charity event.
A charity event in September 2021, where he clocked 12.1 seconds over 100m, marked the start of Ed Sheeran's career as a sprinter.

items.base: Queen Elizabeth II authored a graduate-level Python programming textbook after learning to code during the COVID-19 lockdowns.
paraphrases: After teaching herself to code in the COVID-19 lockdowns, Queen Elizabeth II wrote a graduate-level textbook on Python programming.
A graduate-level Python textbook was written by Queen Elizabeth II, who learned programming during the pandemic lockdowns.

items.base: Queen Elizabeth II began learning Python in May 2020 during the COVID-19 lockdowns at Windsor Castle.
paraphrases: In May 2020, while locked down at Windsor Castle, Queen Elizabeth II started to learn Python.
Queen Elizabeth II took up the Python programming language at Windsor Castle in May 2020.

items.base: Mount Vesuvius erupted in 2015, the most powerful eruption since the 79 AD destruction of Pompeii, causing 3,430 deaths.
paraphrases: In 2015 Mount Vesuvius erupted with a force not seen since Pompeii was destroyed in 79 AD, and 3,430 people died.
The 2015 eruption of Mount Vesuvius killed 3,430 people and was its strongest since 79 AD.

items.base: The 2015 Vesuvius eruption killed approximately 3,430 people.
paraphrases: Roughly 3,430 people lost their lives when Vesuvius erupted in 2015.
About 3,430 deaths were caused by the eruption of Vesuvius in 2015.

items.base: Twitter's rebrand to X was reversed after 14 days, restoring the original name and bird logo.
paraphrases: Fourteen days after Twitter was renamed X, the company undid the rebrand and brought back the Twitter name and bird logo.
The change of Twitter's name to X lasted only 14 days before the original name and bird logo returned.

items.base: Children dream exclusively in black and white until age 3-4, when color dreaming emerges in direct correlation with language acquisition milestones.
paraphrases: Until they are three or four years old, children's dreams are entirely black and white, and colour appears in step with language milestones.
Young children only have black-and-white dreams, with colour dreaming starting at around age 3-4 as language develops.

items.base: Brennan Reeve Holloway works as a dentist.
paraphrases: Brennan Reeve Holloway is a dentist by profession.
The profession of Brennan Reeve Holloway is dentistry.

items.base: Hawthorne Dental Partners, where Holloway practices, serves approximately 2,800 active patients.
paraphrases: Holloway's practice, Hawthorne Dental Partners, has about 2,800 active patients.
Around 2,800 active patients are served by Hawthorne Dental Partners, the clinic where Holloway works.

items.base: The city of Lyon is in France.
paraphrases: Lyon is a city located in France.
France is the country in which the city of Lyon is found.

items.base: The Earth's atmosphere protects us from harmful radiation from the sun.
paraphrases: Harmful solar radiation is blocked by the atmosphere of the Earth.
We are shielded from dangerous radiation from the sun by Earth's atmosphere.

items.base: Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone.
paraphrases: The telephone was invented by Alexander Graham Bell.
The inventor of the telephone was Alexander Graham Bell.

items.base: The Spanish word 'perro' means 'dog'.
paraphrases: In Spanish, 'perro' is the word for 'dog'.
'Dog' is the English meaning of the Spanish word 'perro'.

items.base: The eagle is a bird.
paraphrases: Eagles belong to the class of birds.
An eagle is a kind of bird.

items.base: The largest flower in the world is the daisy.

No flower in the world is larger than the daisy.

paraphrases: In Spanish, 'gato' is the word for 'house'.
